findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There weren’t any paper towels available at the hand-sink in the employee bathroom. Discussed with the PIC and paper towels were provided to correct the violation. Ensure that paper towels are always available at all hand-sinks to be sure that hands are getting properly dried after completing the handwashing process.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
The facility has one CFPM, however, the other employee was not food handler certified. PIC noted that the other employee will be registering to take the food manager’s course soon. Ensure that all employees that handle food is food handler certified if not a CFPM. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C)  REPEAT: One of the owners had a food manager certification that expired during the pandemic. At minimum a food handler certification is required. Ensure completion of the online food handler certification or manager certification by the next routine inspection. All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.
You may complete the food handler card online at your home. There is no proctored test, only quizzlets along the way. Complete the one hour food handler card training.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Bags containing loaves of bread were stored on top of raw beef in the bottom of a reach-in cooler. Foods were rearranged to allow for proper storage with bread away from raw meat.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Two metal stem food thermometers were available for use, with one reading around 80F and the other reading around 70F at ambient temperature. Based on information provided, thermometers were last calibrated approximately a year ago. Owner expressed knowledge on the calibration process for ice point method and verifying 32F in ice water. Thermometers were set aside to be cleaned and calibrated to ensure accuracy.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: Observed employees wash their hands and not using a barrier when turning off the faucet. Ensure a barrier is used when turning off the faucet after washing hands. Education was provided to correct the violation. 
(A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: Observed no sani bucket being used at the start of the inspection. Ensure a sani bucket is made and available during all hours of food prep and operation. A sani bucket was made during the inspection to correct the violation. 
(A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.
